key_insight: The paper introduces a variance-reduction estimator that can track many coupled inner functions using only O(1) stochastic probes per iteration, enabling efficient optimization for finite-sum coupled compositional problems.
engineering_relevance: This is useful for large-scale machine learning systems where objectives are compositional and full inner-function sampling is too expensive, such as multi-task learning and AUC maximization.
method: Proposes Multi-block-Single-probe Variance Reduction (MSVR) to update multiple blocks of g(w) from partial stochastic access.
Builds FCCO algorithms with improved sample complexity across non-convex, convex, strongly convex, and PL settings.
Obtains better dependence on m when outer gradients ∇f_i are linear.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical sample-complexity improvements across multiple objective classes and empirical gains on multi-task deep AUC maximization.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and cost of stochastic oracle access for each block, so implementation may be sensitive when block sampling is highly imbalanced or noisy.
paper_title: Solving Finite-sum Coupled Compositional Optimization via Multi-block-Single-probe Estimator
